Package com.j3d.engine.interact.input.keyboard

Class KeyBindings

java.lang.Object
com.j3d.engine.interact.input.keyboard.KeyBindings
public class KeyBindings extends Object
A class that manages the key bindings for the application. It allows for easy addition and removal of key bindings, and handles the actions associated with each key binding.
Author:
Lehlogonolo Poole

    • childModifiersClash

      public static boolean childModifiersClash(J3Key leader)
      Inspects whether the leader of a chain of keystroke's updated modifier will clash or cause a clash with any 1 child keystroke.

      Preamble : KeyEvent are bit masks, meaning combinations are just the bitwise OR and two combinations such as SHIFT | SHIFT become SHIFT

      In essence a conflict is made when the bitwise OR of the leader's modifiers with any child modifier is equal to the leader modifier. 

      
          (leaderMod | childMod) == leaderMod

      Say we have the following test cases, where the first keystroke is the leader and the rest are childrten. 

      
      1. (I) -> (SHIFT + I) -> (CTRL + I)
      2. (P) -> (ALT + P) -> (SHIFT + P)
      3. K -> (CTRL + K) -> (ALT + K)
      And we'd like to rebind the leader of each link to ALT + O, SHIFT + S and CTRL + ALT + J respectively. (We Only care about the SHIFT, CTRL, ALT, ALT_GRADE and META modifiers, so the letters themselves will be ignored and replaced with a question mark to represent the letter)

      In link 1 it becomes 

      
          (ALT + ?) -> (SHIFT + ALT + ?) -> (CTRL + ALT + ?)
      No child's modifier conflicts with the leader key's modifier. This is a valid change.

      In link 2 

      
          (SHIFT + ?) -> (ALT + SHIFT + ?) -> (SHIFT + SHIFT + ?)
          // The 2 shifts simplify to a singular shift via bitwise OR
          (SHIFT + ?) -> (ALT + SHIFT + ?) -> (SHIFT + ?)
      Here due to the simplification, the leader conflicts with the last child. This is an invalid case.

      In link 3 

      
          (CTRL + ALT + ?) -> (CTRL + CTRl + ALT + ?) -> (ALT + CTRL + ALT + ?)
          // Again the duplicate shifts OR together
          (CTRL + ALT + ?) -> (CTRL + ALT + ?) -> (CTRL + ALT + ?)
      This link, obviously also produces conflicts, accept both children conflict with the parent node.

      And this method, simply checks for these.
      Parameters:
      leader - The leader in question.
      Returns:
      Whether any child modifier of this key clash with said key or not.
